clue.text: Happy to draw in Foreign Office facing America

indicators.note: 'draw in' places the verb inside the Foreign Office abbreviation, so in signals one piece going within another

parts.note: FO is the standard abbreviation for the Foreign Office, Britain's foreign ministry
to draw out a response is to elicit it
US is the United States, i.e. America

explanation.surface: A diplomat is pleased to bring the Foreign Office round to facing the Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicitous is a formal word for well chosen, fortunate or happy, as a happy phrase is an apt one.

clue.text: Relic of silver-coated ship, conceivably

indicators.note: coated says the ship is covered by the silver layer, one piece wrapped round another

parts.note: silver foil is thin metal sheeting
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An old artefact might, one supposes, come from a silver-plated vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the preserved remains of an ancient organism, a relic of the distant past.

clue.text: Answer is to tuck into meal to get going

indicators.note: tucking into something puts it inside, so one letter goes within the meal

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: The answer is to eat a meal before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' suggests eating, but it places A inside LUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To launch a project or campaign is to start it off, to get it going.

clue.text: No coast clean in resort? Find another resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning to sort the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: If the beaches are dirty at your holiday town, go somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: The question-marked 'resort' is read as re-sort; CLACTON-ON-SEA is a seaside town in Essex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Clacton-on-Sea is an English seaside holiday town, so it is a different resort by example.

clue.text: Girl takes two articles

parts.note: the is the definite article and a the indefinite one
the is the definite article and a the indefinite one

explanation.surface: A young woman picks up a pair of items.
explanation.definitionFit: Thea is a female first name, so a girl by example.

clue.text: A French novelist cuts on the phone, perhaps — that's not usual

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: words heard over a phone line are heard not seen, so the novelist and cuts are taken by their sound

parts.note: a novelist is an author, and cuts is docks, as in docking a tail

explanation.surface: A French writer edits material during a phone call, an odd way to work.
explanation.walkthrough: AUTHOR said aloud gives ORTHO and DOCKS gives DOX.
explanation.definitionFit: Unorthodox means contrary to accepted custom, unconventional, hence not usual.

clue.text: Cliff shows sign of injury

definitions.meaning: a steep rocky crag or cliff face, chiefly in northern England
the mark left on the skin after a wound heals

explanation.surface: A fall from a cliff leaves a lasting mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Two separate senses of one word: a rocky crag on a hillside, and the healed mark of a wound.

clue.text: Mountain top — scale it after a fashion being a climber

indicators.note: after a fashion means in some rough way or other, so the letters are put together loosely in a new order
the top of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Reach a peak by climbing roughly, as a mountaineer would.
explanation.walkthrough: The mountaineering picture misleads: the climber is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a flowering vine that climbs walls and trellises, so a climbing plant.

clue.text: Gambling game permitted during journey

indicators.note: during places the permitted piece within the journey, one inside the other

parts.note: a route is the way taken on a journey
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A betting game is allowed while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino game of chance played on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: South America's custom to follow hound

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
A is a common abbreviation for America
a usage is an established custom or practice
to dog someone is to follow or tail them

explanation.surface: It is the done thing in South America for one person to follow a hunting dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' looks like a charade signal but is the verb DOG; 'hound' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage dog is the British nickname for the dachshund, a breed classed among the hounds.

clue.text: Country landscape Russia provides

indicators.note: the words landscape Russia supply the letters that sit across their junction, so provides marks a concealed run

explanation.surface: A rural landscape is what Russia has to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American nation, so a country by example.

clue.text: Back previous member of low class

parts.note: to second a proposal is to support or back it
former means earlier or previous

explanation.surface: Support a one-time member of the lower orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low class' hints at social rank but means a junior school year.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-former is a pupil in the second form, one of the junior classes at a British school.

clue.text: Egg on broadcast clearly visible

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard spoken, so the phrase for clearly visible is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: something clearly visible is in sight

explanation.surface: Someone urges on a broadcast that can be plainly seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or provoke them into acting, a close synonym.

clue.text: Eagerest to repair poor accommodation on board

indicators.note: to repair something is to fix or rework it, so the letters of eagerest are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is most keen to do up shabby cabins on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship, with the most basic quarters.

clue.text: Cowboy film makes hero a poser

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters of the phrase are made into something new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A Western turns its hero into a show-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse opera is a jokey name for a Western movie, featuring cowboys on horseback.

clue.text: One investigating bugs with crafty sting — mole too

indicators.note: crafty means cunning or artful, so the following words are worked cunningly into a new order

explanation.surface: A sly insect sting, and a mole as well, catch a naturalist's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An entomologist is a scientist who studies insects, the creatures loosely called bugs.

clue.text: Set cut off on ship in coastal region

indicators.note: cut off says the end of the word set is removed

parts.note: aboard means on a ship

explanation.surface: A group is stranded aboard a vessel near the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaboard is the strip of land bordering the sea, a coastline.

clue.text: Left wearing label 'pedantic type'

indicators.note: the label wears the letter for left as clothing, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a sticker is an adhesive label

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist sports a badge calling someone a pedant.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exactness and rules, a fussy perfectionist.

clue.text: Consume individual brand then second to admit mistake

parts.note: to consume food is to eat it
a single individual is one
brand is a literary word for a sword

explanation.surface: Eat a single label's product and then a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brand' suggests a product label, but here it is the old poetic word for a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat one's words is an idiom meaning to retract a statement and concede being wrong.

clue.text: Periodical on the web a great attraction

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a mag is short for a magazine, a periodical
the Net is the internet or World Wide Web

explanation.surface: An online magazine pulls in lots of readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet is anything that draws people strongly, as a crowd-puller does.

clue.text: 'Pet' teacher in college where the law gets taught

parts.note: hen is a term of endearment, like pet, in northern English and Scottish speech
a don is a university or college tutor

explanation.surface: A favourite tutor at college teaches law.
explanation.walkthrough: HENDON, in north London, is home to the Metropolitan Police training college; 'the law' means the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Hendon hosts the police training college, so it is a place where officers of the law are trained.

clue.text: Single composer played part back

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer

indicators.note: back says the word for the part played is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a part played by an actor is a role

explanation.surface: An unmarried composer took a part in a performance again.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man, someone single.

clue.text: Rummage about taking long time

parts.note: for can mean concerning or about, as in a plan for the future
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A search through belongings drags on for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rummage about' looks like one phrase, but 'about' gives FOR; 'taking' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search about for food or supplies, close to rummaging.

clue.text: Steering gear made of hard wood

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
elm is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: A ship's wheel built from tough timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The helm is the tiller or wheel used to steer a ship.

clue.text: Join for the whole year

parts.note: the whole of something is all of it

explanation.surface: Sign up for the full twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to unite or link up with another party, a synonym of join.

clue.text: Resolute Heath comes back dressed like a lord

indicators.note: comes back says the former prime minister's first name is read in reverse

parts.note: Ted Heath was a British Conservative prime minister of the 1970s
peers wear robes trimmed with ermine fur, so they are ermined

explanation.surface: A firm Edward Heath returns to the Lords in robes.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath is not open land but the prime minister Edward (Ted) Heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Determined and resolute both describe someone firmly set on a purpose.

clue.text: Make good curse

definitions.meaning: to mend a hole in a sock or garment by stitching
a mild oath, a euphemism for damn

explanation.surface: Repair damage and swear about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: mending fabric with stitches, and a mild exclamation of annoyance replacing damn.

clue.text: Ian Hislop's oppo leaving university with grasp of second old prime minister

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it, so the trimmed comedian's name closes round the piece for second
leaving says the letter for university departs from the comedian's name

parts.note: Paul Merton is the opposing team captain to Ian Hislop on the BBC panel show Have I Got News for You

explanation.surface: A satirist's TV rival quits university clutching a second prize about a former premier.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Merton and Ian Hislop are the rival captains on the British TV quiz Have I Got News for You. Dropping U gives PALMERTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Palmerston was a 19th-century British prime minister, so a former premier by example.
